probeDesign.liveMechanism: Writes one uniquely named one-shot rule (probe-time-trigger-<uuid>, dueAt=now+~1s) to the *live* EventRuleStore passed by Runtime (dataDir/control/event-rules.json), registers an in-memory ephemeral subscription on the *live* TimeSourceService (no control-store subscription row), drives the *live* TimeSourcePump (explicit wake at baseline and at the due boundary, with automatic ticks also valid), and observes the accepted event through the live EventService with a probe-scope inspector.
probeDesign.reservedScope: Events are accepted in the reserved scope "shiyu-time-probe". No live subscription uses that scope, so the probe event cannot be delivered to any Agent/component handler; only the append-only control event remains. Runtime integration adds this scope to the trusted time-source publisher principal.
probeDesign.identity: Expected event payload {subscriptionId, ruleRevision:1, scheduleRef, occurrence=once:1:<ISO dueAt>, scheduledFor=<ISO dueAt>}; the receipt hashes eventId and reports ticksObserved/pollCycles. Repeat pump ticks are driven twice before cleanup and the event count must stay exactly one.
probeDesign.cleanup: Always removes the ephemeral registration, deletes the live rule entry and its derived time state in a finally block, then re-verifies rule/time-state absence. A cleanup failure is reported in the error/receipt rather than hidden.
probeDesign.appendOnlyTruth: The probe deliberately writes one real time.occurred fact to the live control ledger. Control-store events are append-only; the probe cannot delete it, and it must not claim zero side effects. The receipt field liveDataTouched="control-events-append-only" and sideEffects.controlEventAppended=true/eventDeletable=false make this explicit. Only that control event (plus temporary rule-file entry before cleanup) is written; no Task/Session/budget/Effect/delivery row is created.

hostKit.admission: Same session.probe semantics: rejected while globally paused (ensureCanRun), one shared runtime operation slot (capacity 2), abortable, no retry; no model/embedding/Task/Goal/Lab/Effect.

operatorWarnings: This is NOT a zero-side-effect probe: it permanently appends one time.occurred control event. Do not run it as part of a "no business writes" acceptance criterion without recording the exception.

If the process crashes after the rule write but before cleanup, a probe-time-trigger-* entry may remain in dataDir/control/event-rules.json. Without its in-memory ephemeral subscription it cannot fire (readSubscription returns undefined), but the operator should inspect and remove it.
Do not run two live-trigger probes concurrently (tool is non-concurrency-safe); the command also shares the runtime operation slot.

The protected runtime-state file, business Task/Goal/budget/delivery tables and known business Session files must stay unchanged; only the control events ledger gains one time.occurred fact (plus the rule file is transiently rewritten).
stopConditions: Any failed check, any unexpected delivery/business row/model activity, any cleanup failure, or a non-frozen reload => stop, preserve logs, do not retry; the append-only event remains part of the evidence.

gapsAndUntested: runtime.ts/index.ts integration and the fixed-host invocation are NOT executed here; tests use a real temporary ControlStore/EventService/rule file/TimeSourcePump.

The live pump phase in the real host can delay the due tick; the probe relies on explicit pump.wake() at the due boundary (the runtime diff passes this.timePump), so a missing/closed pump makes the probe time out rather than pretending to fire.

Control-store events are append-only: the probe event cannot be removed after the run. This is declared, not a defect; evidence recorders must account for the extra event/delivery counters (no delivery is created because the reserved scope has no subscribers).
Rule-file cleanup requires the rule file to be writable by the runtime; if it is unavailable the probe fails before writing or reports cleanup failure.

No real model/embedding/Task/Effect/Lab/channel was used; this probe proves the live time-source trigger path and the append-only side-effect accounting, not downstream notifications or business scheduling semantics (G4).
Concurrent probes or a crash mid-probe can leave an inert probe rule entry; operator inspection is documented in hostKit.operatorWarnings.
evidenceBoundaries: G1 offline: real temporary SQLite control store + real TimeSourcePump + real temporary rule file + real wall clock. Not fixed-host or business acceptance.
